subject.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine

question: Should OpenClaw core continue toward this built-in `rescueWatchdog` cron/service design, or should the broader Gateway resilience work remain in the canonical issue until maintainers split and sponsor a smaller implementation path?
rationale: The PR adds core recovery automation, service-control behavior, and security-sensitive repair semantics; automation cannot choose the product boundary, upgrade posture, or operator-policy defaults.

options.title: Pause behind the canonical design issue
options.body: Keep the broader Gateway resilience issue as the owner and ask maintainers to split a smaller sponsored PR before reviving this branch.

options.title: Sponsor a rebase and proof pass
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly adopt this PR direction, require a current-main rebase, security review, and real host rescue proof before merge.

options.title: Close and invite a narrow replacement
options.body: If the branch is too stale to salvage, close this PR and invite a fresh PR for one approved piece such as service hardening or rescue payload plumbing.

recommendation.title: Pause behind the canonical design issue
recommendation.body: Keep the broader Gateway resilience issue as the owner and ask maintainers to split a smaller sponsored PR before reviving this branch.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the listed lead maintainer and appears in recent Gateway/daemon history, making him the strongest routing owner for the product/security boundary choice.
